title: Robust Residual Correction via Selective Deployment for Time Series Forecasting
claim: A four-stage pipeline extracts structured features, then fuses a conservative linear correction with a nonlinear one into a final output.
layout: 4 colored stage panels, left-to-right, legend bottom-left, central summary equation
description: A wide block diagram split into four pastel-colored panels numbered 1 to 4, read left to right. Panel 1 (pink), Data Segmentation, shows multichannel time-series input, sliding windows and the resulting segments X_n. Panel 2 (green), Multi-Scale Prior Extraction, feeds X into mean and standard-deviation branches (F_mu, F_sigma). A teal trapezoid labeled Graph Aggregation merges them with a standardization block into F. Panel 3 (orange), Direction-Aware State Encoding, has two parallel branches (Self Pairs, Neighbor Pairs). Each branch has Linear layers, a residual add and Norm, and the branches join into Z. F and Z are concatenated into F'. Panel 4 (blue), Hybrid Residual Correction, splits into a Linear Floor Ridge Regression branch (covariance matrix, cross-term, weights W) and an Adaptive MLP Correction branch (embedding, Linear, GELU, attention). A central equation Y = ŷ + Σ(α r_lin + β r_δ) sits between them, and a gating symbol produces the output Y. A symbol legend sits at bottom-left.
caption: Overview of the CRC framework. CRC first extracts structured residual representations, then proposes conservative and conditional correction components, and finally applies a validation-calibrated deployment rule that deploys corrections only when held-out evidence supports them.
abstract: Post-hoc residual correction can reduce forecasting error, but always-on updates often fail to generalize: when residual signals are weak or noisy, expressive correctors can overfit and even increase the overall forecasting errors. We introduce CRC, a robust residual correction framework that couples a hybrid corrector with a validation-calibrated selective deployment rule. CRC proposes corrections via a conservative ridge "floor" plus conditional nonlinear refinement, but deploys them only when held-out evidence indicates net error reduction over a frozen baseline forecaster. CRC treats when to revise a forecast as a validation-calibrated deployment decision, not only how to fit residuals. Across standard long-sequence benchmarks and multiple backbones, CRC improves horizon-averaged MSE and MAE in most dataset-backbone pairs, with particularly large gains on complex datasets (e.g., over 20% relative MSE reduction on Traffic). We additionally report the non-degradation rate (NDR) as a stability diagnostic of harmful updates and ablate the validation-calibrated "firewall" that stabilizes MSE gains.
